fills.reason: The AES key used to encrypt expense notes is a byte array hardcoded in the app, so anyone with the APK can decrypt stored notes.
OkHttp logging interceptor at BODY level logs full request and response bodies, including login credentials and tokens. I did not confirm whether it is limited to debug builds.
The only WebView sets allowContentAccess to false.
The only WebView sets allowFileAccess to false.
Only keyboardOptions with Email/Decimal types were found; the note field and other inputs were not fully reviewed for suggestion/autocorrect caching of sensitive text.
No FLAG_SECURE or setRecentsScreenshotEnabled found in the code. Whether the expense screens need screenshot protection is a product decision.
No notification APIs (NotificationCompat, NotificationManager) found by searching all app and sync sources.
The login password field uses OutlinedSecureTextField, which masks input and disables suggestions.
A JavaScript interface exposing the session token is added to a WebView that loads a URL taken from an intent/deep link, so any page it loads can read the token.

fills.reason: No filterTouchesWhenObscured or similar overlay protection found; whether it is needed for the login screen is a decision.
Internal navigation uses an explicit Intent(context, HelpActivity::class.java); the other intents are ACTION_SEND/ACTION_VIEW to other apps.
Implicit ACTION_SEND intents carry only a share link and a FileProvider URI with a read grant, both meant to be shared by the user.
No PendingIntent usage found by searching all app and sync sources.
The only deep link uses the custom scheme pennyjar://; there are no https App Links.
The pennyjar://help deep link's 'page' query parameter is passed straight to WebView.loadUrl with no validation or allowlist, and that WebView has the token bridge.

evidence.detail: URL taken from the untrusted deep link.

fills.reason: Share-link tokens are generated with java.util.Random, which is predictable. The links give access to a month of expenses.

evidence.detail: Non-cryptographic RNG used for a security token.

fills.reason: The only seeded Random is in AvatarColors (picks a colour from the name hash), which isn't security-relevant.
Keys are AES-128 (hardcoded note key) and AES-256 (Keystore); no weak sizes found.
Only AES is used for encryption; MD5 appears only to name cache files.
Notes are encrypted with AES in ECB mode, which leaks patterns and has no integrity.
No secure screen lock detection (isDeviceSecure, KeyguardManager) found. Whether the app should require one is a decision.
No asymmetric key pairs (KeyPairGenerator) are used; only AES keys.
Cipher.getInstance is called without an explicit provider.
BiometricPrompt.authenticate is called without a CryptoObject, so the unlock is not bound to a Keystore key; a hooked callback can bypass it.
Keys are not tied to biometrics, so enrollment-change detection (setInvalidatedByBiometricEnrollment) does not apply yet; revisit after fixing MASTG-TEST-0327.
setConfirmationRequired is not set (default requires confirmation); related to the missing crypto binding, a human should review.
No Keystore key uses setUserAuthenticationRequired or validity durations; see MASTG-TEST-0327.
Only BIOMETRIC_STRONG is allowed; there is no DEVICE_CREDENTIAL fallback.
SSLContext.getInstance("TLS") is generic; no old protocols (SSLv3, TLSv1.0/1.1) are requested.
Receipt thumbnails are fetched over plain HTTP.
